subject: Next steps & topology notes from discovery: deployment playbook draft
messages:
From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: elena@stability-finance.com
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-01T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: deployment playbook & high-level topology

Thanks again for taking time today, Elena — good conversation. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before we dive into a technical deep-dive.

Summary of pain / goals you shared
- Primary goal: reduce inference cost while meeting strict latency targets for conversational billing flows.
- Current constraint: peak concurrency ~120 QPS for 512-token average responses; 95/99th latency requirement around 80/150 ms respectively.
- Data residency: production data must remain in US regions; testing allowed in eu-west for staging.
- Security: SOC 2 evidence and audit logs required for procurement.

Preliminary model/infra notes (from discovery)
- Preferred model family: Llama2-70B (customer-quantized variants); open to smaller Llama2-13B for burst scenarios.
- Expected avg sequence length: 480 tokens outbound (response), 40 token prompt.
- KV cache reuse across multi-turn sessions is important to hit SLOs.

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive (Solutions + Infra): walk through deployment topologies (dedicated vs private), batching strategies, and KV cache behavior — 60 min.
2) SLO alignment doc: we’ll produce a short playbook with estimated cost per 1M tokens under a few quantization/batching profiles.
3) Security artifacts: you mentioned SOC2 — if you can share the doc we’ll route to Security.

Irene, can you pick 2-3 topology sketches for the deep-dive? Grace, I’ll loop you in on procurement timelines. Elena, are you available Wednesday 2027-08-04 09:00-10:00 PT for the deep-dive?

Attachments: placeholder for example throughput CSV and SOC2 receipt (you can attach on reply).

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

[attachment: example-mtl-reqs.csv (CSV, 14KB)]
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@stability-finance.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: ops@stability-finance.com
Date: 2027-08-01T15:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment playbook & high-level topology

Markus — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming details and adding a couple specifics from our infra/ops side:  

Clarifications / additions
- SLOs: 95th <= 80 ms, 99th <= 150 ms for 512-token responses. These are strict for our primary billing path. If you have separate latency tiers for interactive vs batch, flag that in the playbook.
- Throughput: sustained 120 QPS with hourly peaks to ~200 QPS for short bursts (5–10 minutes).
- Model: we plan to test a quantized Llama2-70B fp16->int8 pipeline; if cost at scale is high we’ll fallback to a sharded Llama2-13B for lower-latency critical paths.
- Data residency: production only in us-west-2 and us-east-1 — no cross-region fallbacks for production traffic. Staging can be eu-west-1.

Security artifacts: attaching our SOC2 summary and a small CSV with sample QPS distributions. Also please send any questions your security team will require (IAM, KMS, audit-log retention window).

Deep-dive availability: Wed 2027-08-04 09:00 PT works for us. Add a calendar invite to confirm.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
VP, Platform Ops | Stability Finance
elena@stability-finance.com

[attachment: stability_soc2-summary.pdf (PDF, 320KB)]
[attachment: sample-qps-distribution.csv (CSV, 4KB)]
From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: elena@stability-finance.com
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-01T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment playbook & high-level topology

Appreciate the rapid reply and the attachments — I received stability_soc2-summary.pdf.

Irene & team — based on Elena’s numbers I’ll prepare three topology sketches for the deep-dive:
A) Hosted Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated) — single-region pinned pool in us-west-2 with burst capacity to us-east-1 for non-PROD testing. Emphasis: predictable throughput, RAID-style model replication for 99th ms.
B) Private VPC (customer-managed infra) — recommended for tighter network control and KMS/HSM integration; we’ll note tradeoffs on peak scaling and operational ownership.
C) Hybrid split-traffic — critical billing path pinned to dedicated low-latency nodes + overflow to cost-optimized quantized instances for less critical queries.

Checklist for the DWG (before Wed):
- Irene: prepare latency curves (95/99) for each topology under 120/200 QPS profiles and include token-level cost estimates.
- Security: I’ll send the security questionnaire that typically accompanies SOC2 evidence — Elena, please confirm the retention window for audit logs (you mentioned 365 days?).
- Ops: Grace, can you prepare a draft mutual action plan (MAP) with procurement milestones so we can tie technical decisions to contract timing.

I’ll send an invite for Wed 09:00 PT (60 min) and attach the three sketches as PDFs.

Best,
Markus

Thanks all — invite received and confirmed for Wed 09:00 PT. Quick answers in advance of the meeting:
- Audit log retention: 365 days is correct for our procurement baseline. If you require longer for debugging, we can discuss an extended window as an add-on.
- KMS: we will require bring-your-own-key (BYOK) support in any Private option; Dedicated is acceptable with a customer-managed CMK in the cloud provider.

See you Wednesday.
